summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Factor V Leiden deficiency, chronic anticoagulation with Lovenox, incisional hernia, and tracheobronchomalacia was admitted for new-onset right lower quadrant abdominal pain and persistent hemoptysis. The abdominal pain, worsened by movement and poorly controlled on prior oxycodone, was evaluated with CT imaging which showed a small, stable incisional hernia without acute findings. Surgery recommended medical management and outpatient follow-up. Pain was managed with increased oxycodone, acetaminophen, and tizanidine. Hemoptysis and chronic cough were assessed with bronchoscopy, which confirmed tracheobronchomalacia and severe GERD, prompting an increase in PPI therapy. The patient improved clinically, was discharged home on optimized pain and reflux regimens, and advised to follow up with primary care and surgery if symptoms persist.
